caption: : Avg. performance across 11 datasets (y-axis) consistently improves as the number of training examples increases (x-axis). Max is 29k examples, the full size of our dataset.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the average performance across 11 datasets and the number of training examples, with the x-axis labeled “# of training dataset (k)” ranging from 5 to 30 in increments of 5, using a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “Average Performance,” ranges from 48 to 56 in increments of 2, also on a linear scale. A single black line with solid circular markers connects five data points, showing a consistent upward trend. At 5k training examples, the average performance is approximately 48; it increases to about 50 at 10k, 52 at 20k, and reaches approximately 56 at 30k, which corresponds to the maximum size of the training dataset used. The line is solid and smooth, indicating a steady improvement in performance as the training set size grows.
